args: In libjxl/lib/jxl/icc_codec.cc, what safe/fallible varint decoding API is available in this repository that can guarantee a varint is fully contained within a specified byte range such as commands_end? Please provide definitions/signatures and representative callers. Also explain DecodeVarInt behavior on truncated input.

I am fixing the reported 32-bit heap OOB in UnpredictICC at libjxl/lib/jxl/icc_codec.cc:279-287. The function currently calls DecodeVarInt(enc, size, &cpos) for command-stream values even though commands_end may be less than size, allowing a malformed varint to consume data-stream bytes. Predict's uint64_t num is then implicitly narrowed by CheckOutOfBounds and PaddedBytes allocation on 32-bit, while loops retain the uint64_t comparison. Similar command-stream calls exist for numtags, tag offsets/sizes, Insert count, Shuffle count, Predict stride/count. I need the idiomatic root-cause fix, likely a checked decoder bounded by commands_end plus CheckIs32Bit before size_t use.

args: Why might the editing environment classify libjxl/lib/jxl/icc_codec.cc as a fuzzer harness, and is there another non-harness source path or generated/upstream counterpart where UnpredictICC should be patched? Confirm the exact repository-relative location and whether tools/icc_codec_fuzzer.cc is the actual harness.

The vulnerability is explicitly in UnpredictICC in libjxl/lib/jxl/icc_codec.cc. I successfully read that production decoder source, while the sanitizer call stack identifies libjxl/tools/icc_codec_fuzzer.cc as the harness. However, two apply_patch attempts against libjxl/lib/jxl/icc_codec.cc were rejected with the message that it is a fuzzer harness file. The intended changes are a fallible bounded DecodeVarInt helper and checked command count narrowing. I need to distinguish an environment path/classification issue from an actual alternate implementation location.
